reviews.text: 傻福卡表我燥称冯了个福的 你爹第一时间来为你送上专属差评了 吃到真史了，连百龙夜行都不如 主线流程前期无聊中期让我眼前一亮以为只是内容释出慢后面可能就好起来了，结果后面开始全是换皮的单一机制 压轴关甚至是连战前面打过的所有boss战，一点变化没有，这更是坨上加坨😓 最终boss除了有个二阶段没看出有何特色或者区别于普通关普通boss的地方，场地甚至还是直接一个单纯的圆圈大平地 一阶段带村民塔防，机制跟前面的关卡机制一模一样，初见就让我觉得他在逼我固定一种打法 二阶段1v1更是无聊的一批,boss的招式总共4招，一只手数完还能有多😓而且直接就是0交互，长时间施法，玩家想躲就要一直跑，跑完才能蹭两刀普攻，想高输出就只有等技能cd打爆硬直条，真看不出二阶段solo的意义何在，想用1v1solo强调动作塔防里的动作的话，结果就做出这么个玩意未免有点太搞笑了卡普空，我甚至一时想不到哪款游戏的boss战来和他比烂以形容他烂的程度[热] 二周目貌似有隐藏boss和真结局，但我已经忍不了了，勾史啊！！ 游玩卡普空的游戏中的唯一真史，玩了这个之后，之前被我骂史的游戏我看着都顺眼了我燥

This game is SO close to being incredible, but the simplicity of the combat and the ease of most levels betrays it. There's far, far too many levels where you can basically just camp in one spot and lazily do the same attack over and over when a guy walks by. The game is very afraid of throwing too many of the enemy types at you at once, and it results in a very action anemic experience where you spend more time waiting than anything. The downtime in this game is legitimately insane, I can't believe it got past the design phase. First off, you have preparations. So, ok, you have to run around a small level purifying sections of the map to gather villagers and upgrades. This isn't TOO bad, the animations get tiring and you don't have a sprint but if this was all I wouldn't mind. But for some godawful reason, they decided once you beat a level you have to go back into the map and run around it again so you can command the villagers to repair buildings. Some of these buildings give vital upgrades, and you get a unique piece of gear when all upgrades are done. So you set the villagers to do maybe a third of the building tasks, because there's a limited number of them. And then you go off and do a mission. And then you have to go back and run back to the spots again to claim the rewards. And then you have to run around to the other repair points, because you can't reassign villagers until you claim your reward. And then you have to do it again, and ALSO there will be some random planks of wood scattered around that you have to command the villagers to grab for some of the repairs. And then you do it one more time, and then you have to run into a tent on the map to claim the final prize. The end result is you're running around each map a half dozen times doing essentially nothing, because yes you have to do this for EVERY LEVEL. There's also brief boss arenas where you fight one big foe and don't have to do any of that. But they also have a time trial element, where you assign all your units before the fight and then go in. If you screw up the time trial? You're assigning 6+ guys individually again, because there's no option to restart from the fight. In one of these you have 12 guys and the time trial is extremely tight. All of this adds up WAY too much. Last note, you can't rebind a lot of buttons properly. The command button has to be on a bumper or trigger, even though it's not a button that needs to get pressed urgently basically ever. Because of this, the default control scheme has dodge on click left-stick and it's a big pain in the ass to find a configuration where you're not giving up something. If command could be set to up on the d-pad, problem would be solved. But that has to be taken up by the photo mode button that almost no one ever uses. Edit: I made it halfway into new game+ now and yeah, this game just never gets even remotely difficult. There's a small period of time in the last few levels where the game gets hectic enough to be fun (but still not challenging) and then new game+ just gets easier again despite you now having even more upgrades. The only semi-hard thing is doing some of the don't get hit / don't let Yoshiro get hit challenges but they're not actually difficult, they just encourage you to play super safe and lame. Maybe I'd recommend this game if they add some endgame DLC or crazy master levels or something, but as for now the monotony is not worth the few moments of fun it provides. Edit 2: It seems at some point they made it so you can rebind command to left-stick click which fixes that one problem. Campaign is still trash, might try the roguelike mode and see if it's decent. Skeptical.

I want to like this game, I love tower defense but this game just doesn't hit the itch. My biggest issue with the game is the map design, the game desperately needs proper lanes or funnels where you can set up defenses, the later levels become an absolute mess of enemies spawning from 4 different directions with levels that are too open, so the winning strat is putting all your characters around the shrine maiden in a circle. It doesn't really feel like a tower defense game. Along with that there are a lot of (in my opinion) useless characters or classes that do the same thing with different flavor, the sumo wrestler is almost detrimental to you because he constantly pushes enemies out of range, the marksman is a more expensive archer that does more damage while shooting slower, to the point I can't tell if there's even any difference in their dps, especially since the archer is far cheaper to max out in the skill tree. Same exact thing with the lumberjack and the spearman. There are definitely things to like about this game and I hope it gets polished, it's just really not worth 50 euro and considering the peak player counts on steam I feel like this game will be abandoned fairly quickly.

今天打了几关突然觉得好疲惫好索然无味，除了地形和机制的些许差距，每一关都是换汤不换药的换皮重复。 问题也很多，浅列几个比较受不了的： [list] [*]打击感真的不行，吞键很严重。崛起打百龙夜行起码我拿个扩散轻弩下去扫射很爽呢，这里太刀几个招式平砍毫无爽快感。宗的弓箭手感也和*一样，有时候明明LT键长按了还是无法蓄力拉弓，而且按了索敌键也容易胡乱索敌，强扭视角。 [*]关卡内升级村民要结晶，开辟灵道要结晶，有时候世代被控制还要献祭起码2000+结晶。结晶不是一关一结而是延续传承下来，这导致后期结晶非常稀缺，需要靠每一个[b] 已修缮 [/b]的据点供给。但为什么每次收取结晶都需要进入据点再钻进帐篷内找世代？前期还好，后期十几个据点每次都要点进去，你当QQ农场偷菜呢？在关卡选择界面一键收取不就好了，非要刻意拉长游戏时长。 [*]继续上一点说的已修缮据点，没有修缮好的据点还不提供结晶。修缮一个据点起码要打2-3关，有的时候大一点的据点要4关。而且每次据点里一个地方修缮好的奖励也要进去绕路领取，为什么不设置和结晶一起一键收取啊，真的很烦啊！！！ [*]村民职业强度不平衡、中途无法换魔像和装备、失败不能洗点要回帐篷洗等等一系列拖延时长的设定暂且不表，你每一关要完成三个特殊条件才能满纸鹤（满星的意思），那为什么在一开始不告诉我？非要我打一遍才解锁特殊条件，非要我再打一遍。而且 前期的装备根本没办法完成特殊条件，就是非要中期回去刷前期的关卡。 [*]看其他评测说boss关是把前面打的所有小boss汇聚起来马拉松，我无语了，前面有些小boss有多粪你不懂吗CAPCOM？还看到打一周目是一个结局，打二周目才是真结局，一周目我坚持下去都困难了，我真的没办法想我去受第二次折磨。拜拜我走人了 [/list] 打这个游戏真的好像上班，打开电脑想玩点轻松的，想起来Kunitsu还没打完；和朋友打怪猎打到一半，想起来Kunitsu还没打完；周末晚上躺床上了想看个无脑言情，突然想起Kunitsu还没打完，据点还没修好啊，不能休息啊！ 说点好的吧，美术非常非常优秀，完全符合我的审美。女主世代很可爱，萌得我母性泛滥。 还要感谢我对Okami爱得太深，才能为了几首联动BGM坚持到现在= = 希望今年能打完吧

I want to recommend this game, but I can't in good conscience do so. I really appreciate what it does, it's very unique but it's oh so INCREDIBLY tedious, by design. It's a 4 hour game stretched to 14+, in which I have no interest to play or do everything over again. The closest game similar to it that it reminds me of is Brutal Legend, the 2013 game starring Jack Black as the voice of the main character. A mix of RTS/tower defense but with a huge emphasis on an individual, generic two button combat system which I feel just falls completely short. The combat has no depth outside of doing the same combo over and over, which you can later upgrade into a slightly stronger but much slower version of the same combo, that also damages the enemies' stun bars. Having to rely on your main character and not the units you command makes some of the boss fights feel terrible. In fact, most of the bosses just feel like an absolute drag. I found myself stuck in between not understand what I'm supposed to do to deal damage for some, and completely demolishing others with no effort. The difficulty is all over the place. Now for my main real complaint, and the reason I do not recommend it, despite liking some of the ideas and liking the overall theme. The tedious design. Let me give you an example, the game is structured in stages. Each stage has 3 extra objectives which give you extra rewards, but you cannot know what those extra objectives are until after you clear the stage. You might think that's not a big deal right? Just look it up online if you really care to get those on the first try. Well, it's not just about that, you simply CANNOT get those objectives done on the first try. The very first stage has an objective of "deploy 3 different units" and at the time you get to do the stage, you only have two units available. You only unlock the third after clearing it, and the boss. Why did it have to be like this? It's a complete waste of time, just making you play the same stage multiple times to get a little bit more powerful. Now I will admit, I never felt you needed any of those upgrades, I managed to complete the main story without ever worrying about replaying a stage, but it just feels really bad to have those rewards that are impossible to reach dangled over your head. Another point as to why I feel like it's incredibly tedious is the lack of a speed up button while in combat. The stages can take very long to complete, and a lot of that time feels wasted. It being a tower defense hybrid means that you'll sometimes find a setup that just lets you win, but then you just have to wait for the win to be handed to you. You can speed up time while in the setup phase of a stage, but you can't during the combat sections. Why? I feel like there's no reason for it other than tedium. Yet another incredibly tedious mechanic, is the village repairs. Every time you complete a village stage, you are then able to go through the village you've just purified, and assign it's villagers to repair buildings, which will finish repairs after you clear another stage, be it a new one or replaying an old one. This is just incredibly tedious menu gameplay, except it's not even as straightforward as clicking a menu, because you have to walk around a map, walk to the building you want to repair, assign villagers, then come back after a stage to do the same process again while also making sure you've collected the rewards. It is SO ANNOYING and unnecessary. I think about 50% of my total playtime is just me going around towns to interact with buildings. tl;dr, It's a decent game that is unfortunately designed to waste as much of your time as possible

In the opening hours with Kunitsu-Gami (a name I can not remember no matter how hard I try) I was in love. Minimal story getting in the way of gameplay that's wrapped in a lovely art direction with a soundtrack to match. The action/tower defense split has been done before but not enough that I was tired of the mashup, till this game. Kunitsu-Gami has a pretty slow drip feed of new machines to add spice to your journey. A few new villager classes (tower types) and a few twist on a level's normal flow that unfortunately start repeating in the last third or so of the game. The combat is pretty simple and right as it started to wear thing they drop a skill tree on you for Soh, the character you control in direct combat. It's a welcome shot in the arm for the gameplay but it's not a long lasting shot as the progression doesn't actually deepen combat all that much. Worst of all said progression reveals the games worst accepts, and my worst gaming foe, it's inability to respects a gamer's time. There are 2 main sources for the resources needed for upgrades. After completing each stage you can visit the newly restored village and issues repair orders. These orders are completed as you clear, or repeat, stages. Each time you have to go back to each village, each repair spot to collect the rewards and issues more. It's very tedious, there is no options to speed up this process, and you have to do it to stay powerful enough to conquer later stages. The other source of upgrades comes from completing level specific challenges. Challenges that remain hidden till you first clear a stage. While some of these are goals you would try for in the course of normal play, like not taking damage, and might actually complete the first time through. The worse offenders can't even be attempted your first go around. You'll be "challenged" to use let's say 4 different classes when you only currently have access to 3. Come back later and just play the stage again! The game is plenty long enough without all these speed bumps in the game. I know people often push back on games being shorter, thinking they are getting less for their money. Sorry, I bought a toy, not work. Even before the game forced me into a boss rush (oh yeah there are bosses in this, they are ok nothing special save for a handful that are really tedious encounters forcing you to chase your opponent through small areas) the love had faded. When the game ask you to do a complete New Game+ playthrough, with even more challenges per stage, to get the true ending, the love affair was over and I only felt regret. Kunitsu-Gami isn't a bad game by any means despite how negative I am towards it. I was enjoying my time with it, with it's core tower/action defense gameplay. However the game's worst traits are things I'm particularly sensitive too and what causes me to warn others away from it.

作为一款带动作元素的塔防游戏，整体的塔防系统能到9分甚至更高，但是这套动作系统作为添头可能只有及格分，将其嵌入后反而有损整体的游戏体验。整体体验上难度和难度曲线都适中，属于是容易过关但是难于达成一些局内的小任务，角色的职业区分、地图内各种防御设施和地图间的特色设计提升了游戏的战略性，也让整体体验不会过于重复死板。这套动作系统相比之下就显得简陋了，弹反僵直和蓄力攻击等都作为养成需要靠后续加点才能点出来，并且主角的养成系统也比较简陋（甚至把几个自动编阵型的功能都算作主动加点解锁的技能）；战斗体验上比较偏老式，靠轻击和重击点的顺序打连招，除了刀锷基本上也没几种打法，使得有一关主角单人关卡的体验就会显著的更差。 游戏最大的闪光点在于其对日本传统民俗的设计和还原，这不仅仅体现在了艺术品级别的美术设计和视效上，在各个据点解放后的每个npc的介绍上，一些收集品像刀锷、被动道具、绘马、食物上都兼具美学、还原度和统一性，而在闯关中和建设据点过程中的音乐也能完美的和游戏进程融为一体，让玩家的游玩氛围感很出色。 总体而言称不上面面俱到的神作但也至少是一部值得游玩的佳作，希望卡表也能多关注、往祇女神之道如此具有潜力的题材和玩法投入。

ONE OF THE MOST UNIQUE GAMES FROM CAPCOM Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess is one of those games that feels impossible to compare with anything else. It is a strange but incredibly successful mix of tower defense, action combat, RTS and RPG elements, creating an experience that feels completely unique. From the very beginning, the biggest impression is the presentation. This game is not only beautiful it feels like a living Japanese diorama. The amount of detail, the art direction, animations and especially the soundtrack create an atmosphere that is hard to find in modern games. The music deserves special praise. It dynamically changes depending on what is happening during missions, and some tracks stayed in my head long after finishing the game. The whole audio design perfectly matches the ritualistic feeling of cleansing the mountain from demons. The gameplay loop is simple but incredibly addictive. During the day, you prepare the battlefield, rescue villagers, assign them roles and create your defense strategy. During the night, everything changes into a desperate battle where you need to command your units while also fighting alongside them as Soh. Every unit has a different purpose, and creating the right combination is the key to success. The tower defense elements are surprisingly deep, while the action combat gives you direct control over the battle instead of just watching your army fight. I also love how much personality the game has. The enemies, locations and characters feel inspired by Japanese folklore but still create something completely original. Almost every element feels carefully designed. Unfortunately, the Steam Deck experience is not as good. The game is playable, but reaching stable higher framerates is difficult and you should expect around 30 FPS with adjusted settings. My biggest complaints are the resource management between missions and some New Game Plus requirements. The true ending requires replaying the entire game, and while NG+ adds new challenges, some of them feel more like grinding than meaningful new content. Despite these issues, Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess is one of the most memorable games I have played recently. It is creative, beautiful and full of passion. In a market full of safe and similar games, Capcom created something genuinely different. I finished it 100% and I absolutely loved my time with it. Pros: + Extremely unique gameplay combination + Beautiful Japanese inspired art direction + Incredible soundtrack + Fantastic atmosphere + Great mix of tower defense and action combat + Many interesting units with different roles + Creative enemy designs + A lot of passion and attention to detail Cons: - Steam Deck performance could be better - Some grinding is required for upgrades and challenges - True Ending requires a full replay - Some NG+ challenges feel repetitive Highly recommended if you want something completely different from modern AAA games.

The game is a breeze right up until you have to deal with the clunky, awkward parry-heavy fighting mechanics (that they conveniently left out of the demo). Then suddenly you're wondering why you can't animation cancel after your sword has already hit, and why your iframes expire while the same special is ongoing. As for the actual fun part, the tower defense is a smooth and steady experience of adding more problems and solutions, right up until they kill off all your villagers and force you back into dark souls. It took me 40 hours to 100% the game and I'm still fuming after that last boss fight. But can you really condemn a game you've 100%ed? Obviously there's something here that I like. Up until the end, every solution I encountered, I was able to cheese past. Bosses that first throttle you for 7 minutes you can annihilate in under 30 seconds after you upgrade everything. Then the final boss starts stunlocking and OHKing you with ranged attacks every 5 seconds. In short, tower defense is fun, but I don't want to play dark souls. Stop trying to get me to play dark souls.
